[[File:Francesca Biagini (31093).jpg|thumb|Francesca Biagini (2025)]]
'''Francesca Biagini''' (born 31 July 1973) is a German and Italian mathematician{{r|cv}} specializing in [[mathematical finance]], [[stochastic calculus]], and [[probability theory]]. Topics in her research include [[fractional Brownian motion]] and [[portfolio optimization]] for [[insider trading|inside traders]].{{r|formeln}} She is a professor of applied mathematics and vice president for international affairs and diversity at [[LMU Munich]],{{r|cv|vp}} and president of the Bachelier Finance Society.{{r|bach}}

==Education and career==
Biagini was a high school student in [[Pistoia]], and earned a [[laurea]] in mathematics in 1996 from the [[University of Pisa]], under the mentorship of Margherita Galbiati.{{r|cv}} She completed a doctorate in 2001 at the [[Scuola Normale Superiore di Pisa]], with the dissertation ''Quadratic hedging approach for interest rate models with stochastic volatility'' supervised by Maurizio Pratelli.{{r|cv|mg}}

She worked as an assistant professor at the [[University of Bologna]] from 1999 to 2005, when she moved to [[LMU Munich]] as an associate professor. After declining an offer to become a chaired professor at the [[University of Hanover]] in 2008, she was given a chair as full professor of applied mathematics at LMU Munich in 2009.{{r|cv}}

She became vice president for international affairs and diversity at LMU Munich, and is president of the Bachelier Finance Society for the 2020–2021 term.{{r|cv}}

==Books==
With Massimo Campanino, Biagini is the coauthor of ''Elementi di Probabilità e Statistica'' (Springer, 2005), an Italian-language textbook on [[probability theory]] and [[statistics]] translated into English as ''Elements of Probability and Statistics: Introduction to Probability with the De Finetti's Approach and to Bayesian Statistics'' (Springer, 2016).{{r|eps}} With Yaozhong Hu, [[Bernt Øksendal]], and Tusheng Zhang, she is the coauthor of the [[monograph]] ''Stochastic Calculus for Fractional Brownian Motion and Applications'' (Springer, 2008).{{r|scfb}}

==Recognition==
Biagini was awarded the Princess Therese of Bavaria Prize, an award for outstanding women scientists at [[LMU Munich]], in 2019.{{r|ptb}}
